sections.h2: Where is Fulton County and which offices handle its property tax?
sections.html:
Fulton County lies in west central Illinois along the Illinois River valley, with Lewistown as the county seat and Canton as the largest city. It was organized in 1823 out of Pike County and covers 883 square miles, of which 866 are land. Property tax for a house here runs through three offices: the Treasurer (who is also the ex-officio County Collector), the Supervisor of Assessments, and the Board of Review, whose clerk is the Supervisor of Assessments.

Both offices sit in the Fulton County Courthouse, 100 N. Main Street, Lewistown. The county's cities and town are Canton, Cuba, Farmington, Lewistown and Astoria, and the county touches Warren, Knox, Peoria, Tazewell, Mason, Schuyler and McDonough counties. A house in Canton and one near Astoria are billed by the same Treasurer.

  • Treasurer/Collector: PO Box 111, Lewistown, IL 61542, phone (309) 547-3041 ext. 132, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm.
  • Supervisor of Assessments: PO Box 283, same courthouse, phone (309) 547-3041 ext. 113, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm with no lunch closure.
  • Township assessors set values in the townships that have one. In the others, county deputy assessors do the yearly fieldwork.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about homes in Fulton County?
sections.html:
Fulton County is a lower-priced, slowly shrinking market. The Census Bureau estimates 32,901 residents for July 1, 2025, a drop of 2.3% from the April 2020 base, and counts 15,869 housing units. Owner-occupancy is 76.6%, and 23.7% of residents are 65 or older.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home (2020 to 2024): $107,200.
  • Median gross rent: $785. Median household income: $60,599.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 18.
  • Average commute to work: 25.8 minutes.

With values in that range, an unpaid tax bill or a long repair list takes a bigger bite out of a sale than it would in a county with higher prices.

sections.h2: How is a Fulton County tax bill figured?
sections.html:
The Treasurer's bill insert gives the formula: equalized assessed value (EAV), minus exemptions, times the total local tax rate equals the bill. The EAV is typically 33 1/3% of fair market value, adjusted by a state-mandated multiplier. The major taxing bodies are school districts, the county, municipalities, townships and special districts such as park, library, fire protection and sanitary districts.

The Treasurer's page describes the scale of the roll. For the 2023 levy payable in 2024, about 26,500 bills went out, the extension was over $55 million, and distributions went to 122 taxing bodies. Net taxable value for that roll was $640,830,290 after $98,623,839 of exemptions. Distributions to the taxing bodies are made every 30 days from the first due date.

Fulton County bills a year behind. Taxes on the 2024 assessment were mailed in 2025, with the first installment due June 13 and the second due September 5, per the Treasurer's report to the County Board. Both dates have passed. Each year's bill carries two payment stubs, and a missing bill does not excuse the owner from paying. Ask the Treasurer for the installment dates printed on the current bill.

sections.h2: How and where can a Fulton County bill be paid?
sections.html:
The Treasurer takes payment in person, by mail, at most county banks, in a courthouse drop box, online and by phone. Cash, personal checks, cashier's checks, money orders and cards are accepted at the counter, and cards carry a convenience fee. Each channel stops working at a different point in the year, which matters for anyone paying after a closing date slips.

Fulton County payment channels and cutoffs (source: Fulton County Treasurer, Payment Options page)
ChannelWhat the county says
Courthouse counterMonday to Friday, 8:00 am to 4:00 pm; bring the stubs
MailMust be postmarked on time; a postage meter imprint is not accepted as proof
Local banksOpen during banking hours with stubs; not available once an installment is delinquent
Drop boxBack door of the courthouse; after 2:00 pm the payment takes the next day's date; no cash
OnlineNot accepted after the second installment due date
CardsNot accepted after the second installment due date
Personal checksNot accepted after delinquent certified letters go out in September

The county's 2025 bill insert adds that mail is postmarked when processed, not when dropped off, effective December 24, 2025, so a hand-stamp at a post office counter or an early mailing is safer. Returned checks carry a $25 fee.

sections.h2: What happens if a Fulton County bill is paid late?
sections.html:
Late tax in Fulton County bears interest at 1.5% per month or portion of a month. The bill insert cites 35 ILCS 200/21-15 for that rate and notes that the payment scale on each stub shows the penalty for each date range. Under 35 ILCS 200/21-135 the collector also collects $10 for certified mailing, advertising and publication costs.

  • 35 ILCS 200/20-25 lets the collector refuse a personal or corporate check within 45 days before a tax sale.
  • Unpaid parcels are published and certified letters are mailed, then the Treasurer takes judgment from the circuit court and runs the delinquent tax sale.
  • The Treasurer's tax computation page lists those steps, along with the County Clerk's role in calculating rates and collecting redemptions on sold taxes.

Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure by parcel number before any closing. The county's online property tax inquiry searches by parcel number, owner name, address, sale price or tax code, and it prints the bill and the payment history for each parcel.

sections.h2: How does a Fulton County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
An owner who thinks the value is too high can ask the township assessor or the county deputy assessors for an informal review, then file a complaint with the Board of Review. The complaint window is 30 days after the date of publication for the township, and the publication date changes every year. A tax bill itself cannot be appealed. Once it arrives, only errors of fact such as a missing exemption or wrong square footage can be fixed through the Assessment Office.

The Board of Review rules for assessment year 2025 add details that matter to people in the middle of a sale. The person filing must hold a legal interest at the time, and that includes a recorded deed, a recorded contract for deed or installment memorandum, or a purchase agreement fully signed by both parties. Complaints go in by hand or by mail, courier or parcel service and must be postmarked by the last filing day. The Board does not accept email or fax.

  • Equity appeals compare assessments of similar nearby homes. Market value appeals rest on recent sales of comparable homes.
  • Evidence the county names: a realtor's market analysis, a certified appraisal, a comparable sheet, a closing statement and photographs.
  • After a tentative decision and a hearing, a final notice goes out. Disagreement can go to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board within 30 days of the postmark date on that notice.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can lower a Fulton County bill?
sections.html:
Fulton County lists seven homestead exemptions, and the owner is responsible for applying for each one. The Assessment FAQ tells owners to check the bill every year to confirm they receive all they qualify for.

  • General Homestead Exemption for owner-occupied residences.
  • Senior Citizen Homestead Exemption for owners over 65.
  • Senior Citizens Assessment Freeze Exemption, which holds the assessed value at a base year with income limits. The county stresses that it does not freeze the tax bill amount.
  • Homestead Improvement Exemption for added value from a new improvement on a parcel that also has the general exemption.
  • Returning Veteran's, Disabled Veteran's (at least 50% service-connected disability certified by the VA) and Disabled Persons' exemptions.

A buyer who plans to live in the house should ask the Assessment Office at (309) 547-3041 ext. 113 which filings the new owner must make. A seller who moved out partway through the year should ask the same office how the exemption is handled for that year's bill.

sections.h2: What should a Fulton County seller do about unpaid or unclear tax?
sections.html:
Start with the parcel number, which is printed at the top left of the bill and is also searchable online. Pull the payment history, confirm which installments are open, and ask the Treasurer for the total owed with penalties through the expected closing date. Bring the Assessment Office any exemption that should be on the parcel, because an error of fact can be corrected after the bill is issued.

Houses that need work, carry back taxes or sit in an estate can be hard to sell on the open market at a price near the county's modest median. A direct as-is sale to a cash buyer is one way to close without repairs, and the tax balance is simply settled in the contract. Whichever route you pick, get the payoff in writing from the Treasurer so no installment is left behind.

faqs.q: When are Fulton County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due in two installments, and the dates change each year. For the 2024 taxes payable in 2025 the first installment was due June 13 and the second September 5, and both have passed. Read the stubs on the current bill or call the Treasurer at (309) 547-3041 ext. 132.

faqs.q: Who sends the Fulton County tax bill?
faqs.a: The County Treasurer, who also serves as ex-officio County Collector, prints and mails the bills. The County Clerk calculates the rates first, and the Assessor sets values and approves exemptions. If no bill arrives, contact the Treasurer, because a missing bill does not excuse the tax.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying Fulton County taxes late?
faqs.a: Interest runs at 1.5% per month or portion of a month. The bill insert cites 35 ILCS 200/21-15 for the rate, and a $10 cost for certified mailing and publication applies under 35 ILCS 200/21-135. The payment scale on each stub shows the exact amount for each date range.

faqs.q: How long do Fulton County owners have to appeal an assessment?
faqs.a: The window is 30 days from the publication date for the township, and that date varies by year. Complaints go to the Supervisor of Assessments as clerk of the Board of Review, by hand or by mail with a postmark, never by email or fax. A further appeal to the Property Tax Appeal Board must be filed within 30 days of the final notice's postmark.

faqs.q: Can someone under contract to buy a Fulton County house file an assessment complaint?
faqs.a: Yes, if the purchase agreement for the property is fully signed by both parties. The Board of Review rules list a recorded deed, a recorded installment memorandum, a contract for deed or lease-to-own on file, and a fully executed purchase agreement as qualifying legal interest.
